title: Constant coefficient model and local power-torsion systems
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], represented in a universe containing a commutative ring $A$ by the coefficient-sized model [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $O=\underline A$ be the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with $A$ universe lifted. For an ideal $I\subseteq A$, define its extended module ideal as the kernel of the constant quotient map $O\to\underline{A/I}$ in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The quotient is given its scalar-restricted module structure, and the quotient map sends the unit generator to $1$. Use the standard derived category and its localization functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define derived $I$-completeness by [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete] for this ideal inclusion; degree-zero completeness uses the single complex. An ideal annihilates a module when all its local sections act by zero. A module is locally a power-torsion limit when on each object there is a covering sieve, and on each member its restriction is isomorphic to the inverse limit of a sequence whose level $n$ is killed by the extended ideal $I^{n+1}$. Transition maps are arbitrary. All these are the unchanged constructions previously in TorsionLimitSheafCompleteness.
